Baron Virril

Overview

Baron Virril commands the Canian holdouts on Jigran against Firez’s Khadaganian forces. Proud of his family, he dislikes asking for aid even after losing Dar-Ulgorn. Kir’s arrival, the fight against the undead and the recruitment of powerful allies give his army a chance to attack Firez’s stronghold. He imagines a restored, prosperous Jigran ruled by his descendants. [1, 2, 3]

Return to Jigran and Dar-Leanos

The old portal brings the travellers to the Canian side of Jigran, where Baron Virril questions their arrival amid attacks by the undead. The baron has lost Dar-Ulgorn to Firez’s forces but refuses Kir’s suggestion to seek outside help, citing his family’s pride. Kir and Kel assist the endangered settlements. They meet the baron’s son Dartas and the overworked Master Stark. Stark provides a password for Uncle Rad, a seller of sweets who secretly gathers intelligence for the baron. These local alliances make the campaign against Firez possible. [4, 5, 6, 7, 1, 8, 9]

Jaminin’s experiment and the undead

The trail of the local undead leads to Jaminin on Death Island. Brought before the baron, he bargains for his life with the promise of useful knowledge. Kir and Kel obtain a potion from a tomb, but need to know how to apply it across the affected area. Jaminin first entertains a human sacrifice; Kel rejects it, and he supplies a less destructive method involving cemetery soil and an incantation. The potion puts the dead to rest. His later exchanges preserve the distinction between theoretical learning and practical competence: he possesses information, but his own experiment caused the disaster. [10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15]

Weapons, Dartas and preparations for war

Kir proposes a special weapon alloy against the undead. Stark initially refuses instruction from a youngster and sends him to an abandoned forge, then has to confront the usefulness of the result. The baron welcomes the advantage for his soldiers. A separate conflict with Dartas moves from arrogance and a duel to an admission of fear for his family and Jigran’s future. Kir explains his own history of enslavement and determination to return, winning the young man’s respect. Dartas later becomes a useful source about an amulet from a village destroyed by harpies. [16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22]

Dar-Ulgorn and the river crossing

Uncle Rad’s intelligence and preparations distract the defenders of Dar-Ulgorn so the baron’s forces can retake the fortress. The victory restores the family’s former boundary, but Virril will not advance blindly into Khadaganian territory. Kir and Kel steal a detailed map from the enemy headquarters and deliver Rad’s report. The resulting offensive captures the river crossing and brings Firez within reach. Kel worries that the end of Kir’s family quest will also end their life together, while the baron imagines a prosperous Jigran under his descendants. The victory means different things to the people who share it. [23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, 2, 30]

The Joon cache and allies for the assault

The sealed cache supplies Kir with Joon armour, but Tui-Len warns him against relying on hatred alone. He gives him an amulet that can turn dangerous creatures into allies. Rad identifies suitable hunting grounds for a cyclops and a dragon. Their recruitment changes the military balance and answers the baron’s objection that his soldiers cannot face Firez’s necromancy in a direct assault. Virril finally orders the attack. Before the confrontation, Rad speaks of the quiet home and family he hopes to have when his secret work is finished. [31, 32, 3, 33]
